contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Stiklestad in Trøndelag was the site of the Battle of Stiklestad on 29 July 1030, where King Olaf II Haraldsson of Norway was killed fighting to reclaim his throne from Cnut the Great and his Norwegian allies.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: Olaf's death at Stiklestad transformed a military defeat into a royal martyrdom. Reports of miracles at his burial site at Nidaros led to his canonization in 1031, making him the patron saint of Norway. Stiklestad became a pilgrimage site, and Saint Olaf's cult shaped Norwegian royal ideology and Christian identity for centuries.
